newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Television ask-only in Tokyo morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Television ask-only in Tokyo morning trade.

text.p: Shares in Nippon Television Network Corp were ask-only in Tuesday morning trade after news that a group led by the company was among the successful bidders for three prime tracts of land in central Tokyo on Monday, brokers said.
They said heavy selling orders, especially from foreign investors, were placed at 34,600 yen as of 0110 GMT. The share closed at 35,800 yen on Monday.

"Selling interest emerged on speculation that the company would face added financial burdens after winning the auction on Monday. It was also a surprise that the company won the auction, so that this caused an even bigger stock market reaction," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.

JNR Settlement Corp announced on Monday that idle land located near Ginza, Tokyo's premier shopping district and once a freight station owned by the defunct Japanese National Railways, sold for 372.3 billion yen. The sum exceeded most analysts' expectations.

JNR said successful bidders for the three lots were a group led by Dentsu Inc; a group led by Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd, including Matsushita Electric Works Ltd and Alderney Investment Pte Ltd, and the group led by Nippon Television Network Corp.
